strategy.summary: Add a Playwright smoke suite (tests/smoke.spec.js), every test tagged @smoke in its title, covering the shop's critical paths: health, catalogue, product page, add to cart, cart, checkout and placing an order, plus the refusals on those paths (unknown product, empty cart checkout, empty checkout form). A `test:smoke` script runs only @smoke tests, locally (the config starts the shop) or against a deployed build via BASE_URL.
inScope: Smoke tests of the critical paths with Playwright, tagged @smoke in the title
A test:smoke npm script that runs only @smoke tests
Making the local webServer port configurable so an already running dev shop on 4175 isn't reused
outOfScope: Changing CI or the deployment pipeline (listed as follow-ups)
Automated accessibility (axe) scanning: no axe dependency in the repo and the ticket asks for a critical-path smoke suite
assumptions: The real shop runs (started by Playwright's webServer locally, or the deployed build at BASE_URL); nothing is faked. The shop has no login/access control.

Q1 (asked, unanswered): the place-order test runs when the suite starts the shop locally; with BASE_URL set it is skipped unless SMOKE_PLACE_ORDER=1, so production gets no orders. All other smoke tests are read-only or refused before a request leaves the browser.
Products, names and prices are imported from src/catalogue.js (PRODUCTS, formatPrice), so a deployed build of the same commit matches.
The cart is a browser cookie, so each test's fresh browser context gives it its own cart; the placed order is identified by a per-attempt customer name shown on the confirmation.
openQuestions: Q1: should placing an order run against production, staging, or neither? (assumption above)
Which pipeline step should run `npm run test:smoke` with BASE_URL after each deploy?

risks.description: A smoke run against production creates real orders
risks.mitigation: TC9 is skipped against a deployed build unless SMOKE_PLACE_ORDER=1; TC8 is refused by the browser before any POST is sent and asserts no POST /orders request was made

risks.description: Locally the config reuses a dev server already on 4175, testing stale code
risks.mitigation: webServer uses PORT from E2E_PORT (default 4176, unused by repo scripts)

risks.description: A page renders but a key element (price, total, cart count) is wrong
risks.mitigation: Assert exact prices computed from the catalogue, exact cart count and the exact total line

acceptanceCriteria.text: The shop reports it is up: GET /health returns 200 with {status: 'ok'}
Shoppers can browse the catalogue and open a product page showing its name and price; an unknown product gives a Not found page
Shoppers can add a product to the cart and see the cart with its lines and total
Shoppers can check out and place an order, and get a confirmation; checkout is refused with an empty cart or missing details
Every smoke test is tagged @smoke in its title and the smoke suite can be run on its own, against a local or deployed build

review.standard: General test automation standards: an absence check first asserts on something that must be there; e2e: a refusal test proves the refusal for the reason it sets up
review.summary: TC8 doesn't prove the browser blocked the submit: `validity.valueMissing` is true for any empty required field whether or not the click was refused, and the URL check and the `orderRequests` check run straight after the click, before a submit started by that click would have navigated or fired its request event.
review.failureScenario: Say the form gets `novalidate`, or the button gets `formnovalidate`. The browser then submits the empty form, and the server places an order with no details (server.js:36-40 doesn't validate) and redirects. In the test, `valueMissing` still evaluates to true. `toHaveURL('/checkout')` passes on its first poll because the navigation hasn't committed yet. `orderRequests` is checked synchronously, before the request event arrives. So the test passes while the refusal is broken. A fix: assert the observable effect of a blocked submit (`await expect(name).toBeFocused()`, since the browser focuses the first invalid field), then check that the order summary is still shown before checking that no POST was sent.

review.standard: follow_up: a claim in a comment the changes add that the files it describes contradict
review.summary: The comment says that against a deployed build, order-placing tests are skipped unless SMOKE_PLACE_ORDER=1. But the existing tests/checkout.spec.js places an order and has no @places-order tag, so `npm run test:e2e` with BASE_URL set still creates real orders.
review.failureScenario: Someone trusts the comment and runs `BASE_URL=https://prod… npm run test:e2e`. grepInvert drops only @places-order, so checkout.spec.js's 'places an order for what is in the cart' runs and places a real production order. `test:smoke` is safe only because its --grep @smoke leaves out the untagged spec. Fix: tag that test @places-order too, or reword the comment so it only covers @smoke runs.

refusals.reason: tests/smoke.spec.js written before testforge:api, testforge:implementation were loaded
yarn.lock isn't a file the run added: delete_file deletes only those.
An independent review of your changes found 1 blocking problem(s).

questions.question: The smoke suite will run against staging and production (BASE_URL). Placing an order (POST /orders) is the only thing that changes server state. Should the @smoke test that places an order run against deployed builds, including production?
questions.assumption: The place-order smoke test runs when the suite starts the shop locally. Against a deployed build (BASE_URL set) it is skipped unless SMOKE_PLACE_ORDER=1 is set, so staging can opt in and production gets no orders. Every other smoke test only reads, or is refused before any request goes out, so it is safe to run anywhere.
questions.answer: No preference from the reviewer: decide yourself from the code, record the decision as an assumption and carry on.
